code.title: RAII Stack Simulator
code.description:
A controller class demonstrates RAII-style resource management: the constructor grabs a heap array and the destructor gives it back. Define class IntStack with an int pointer data, a capacity cap and a top index. The parameterized constructor allocates the array with new and prints 'Stack allocated with capacity <cap>'. push(v) prints 'Pushed <v>', or 'Stack overflow' when the stack is already full; pop() prints 'Popped <v>' where v is the most recently pushed value, or 'Stack underflow' when the stack is empty. The destructor releases the array with delete[] and prints 'Stack memory released'. Read the capacity and the number of operations k, then process k operations in order, each being the word push followed by an integer v, or the word pop.

Input Format:
First two integers: capacity and k. Then k operations separated by spaces: push v or pop.

Output Format:
One line per event in order, starting with 'Stack allocated with capacity <cap>' and ending with 'Stack memory released'.

Constraints:
1 <= cap <= 10; 1 <= k <= 20; 0 <= v <= 1000

mcqs.title: What a Constructor Does

mcqs.Option1: A member function that must be called manually after creating an object
mcqs.Option2: A special member function that is invoked automatically when an object is created
mcqs.Option3: A function that destroys an object at the end of the program
mcqs.Option4: A keyword used to declare a class

mcqs.title: Constructor Name and Return Rule
mcqs.description: Which rule about a constructor's name and return type is correct?
mcqs.Option1: It must have the same name as the class and may return int
mcqs.Option2: It can have any name but must return void
mcqs.Option3: It must have the same name as the class and has no return type, not even void
mcqs.Option4: It must be named init and return the object

mcqs.title: Default Constructor Purpose
mcqs.description: The default constructor is the constructor that:
mcqs.Option1: Can be called with no arguments and gives the object its initial state
mcqs.Option2: Takes exactly one argument
mcqs.Option3: Copies one object into another
mcqs.Option4: Runs only when the program ends

mcqs.title: Why Destruction Runs in Reverse
mcqs.description: Why does C++ destroy objects in the reverse order of their construction?
mcqs.Option1: The compiler reverses the order to save memory
mcqs.Option2: Destructors must run in alphabetical order of class names
mcqs.Option3: An object created later may depend on an earlier one, so reverse unwinding destroys dependents before the resources they rely on
mcqs.Option4: Reverse order applies only to objects created with new
